record.paper_title: Open Questions Related to Bose-Einstein Correlations in e+e− → Hadrons
record.context_brief: experimental validity of Generalised Bose-Einstein Correlations
record.original_question: Can Bose-Einstein correlations in high-energy hadron production be consistently generalized by imposing isospin invariance, so that a Generalised Bose-Einstein Correlation framework relates systems such as π±π± and π±π⁰, and can this GBEC framework be experimentally verified in high-energy physics?

evidence.quote: In analogue to the generalised Pauli principle, which extends that principle from two identical nucleons to the proton-neutron system, one may consider an inclusions of the isospin invariance to extend the BEC to a generalised BEC (GBEC).
Such an extension has been proposed by several authors [1] with the aim to establish BEC relations between e.g. the π±π± and π±π0 systems.
The GBEC validity at high energy physics is still an open question due to the missing of an experimental verification.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Bose–Einstein correlations (BEC) describe the enhancement, at small four-momentum difference Q, of the joint production probability of pairs of identical bosons (e.g. π±π±) in high-energy multiparticle final states, arising from the symmetrization of the two-boson wave function. By analogy with the generalised Pauli principle, which extends antisymmetrization from two identical nucleons to the proton–neutron isospin doublet, one may attempt to incorporate isospin invariance into BEC to obtain a Generalised Bose–Einstein Correlation (GBEC) framework. In this framework, when a pair of pseudoscalar mesons belonging to the same isospin multiplet (such as the pion triplet) is produced, together with its accompanying hadrons, from an overall isosinglet (I=0) source, symmetrization in the combined space–isospin variables would predict definite relations between the low-Q correlation functions of non-identical charge combinations (such as π±π⁰) and those of identical pairs (such as π±π±, π⁰π⁰).

Problem. Formulate a consistent GBEC framework for high-energy hadron production (in particular e⁺e⁻ → hadrons) by imposing isospin invariance, deriving from it quantitative relations between the two-particle BEC functions C₂(Q) of the π±π± and π±π⁰ systems (and, more generally, of mesons in a common isospin multiplet produced from an I=0 source). Then determine whether such GBEC predictions can be experimentally established at high energies, by identifying observables and event selections (ensuring an I=0 initial subsystem) for which the predicted relations between π±π⁰ and π±π± (or analogous K±K⁰ and K±K±) correlation functions can be tested, and assess whether existing or feasible measurements confirm the framework.
artifact.status_search_result: The theoretical GBEC framework relating π±π± and π±π⁰ (and K±K± with K±K⁰) via isospin invariance has been proposed (Alexander–Lipkin, 1999) and some related measurements of π⁰π⁰ BEC at LEP exist, but no direct experimental verification of the GBEC relations between non-identical isospin partners (e.g. π±π⁰) at high energies is reported. A recent BESIII prospects paper (2024) still discusses such tests as future possibilities, indicating the question remains experimentally open.

status_evidence.title: Isospin Invariance and Generalized Bose Statistics applied to Low energy K±K0 and π±π0 space symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Extends BEC of identical bosons in K+K+, π+π+ to K±K0 and π±π0 pairs when produced from an I=0 initial state.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical GBEC framework relating identical and non-identical isospin partners has been proposed.

status_evidence.title: Bose–Einstein correlations of π0 pairs from hadronic Z0 decays
status_evidence.snippet: Measurement of BEC for π0π0 pairs in Z0 decays.
status_evidence.claim: Some related experimental measurements (π0π0) exist, but not direct tests of GBEC π±π0 vs π±π± relations.

status_evidence.title: Principles and prospects of Bose-Einstein correlation study at BESIII
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses prospects for testing isospin-based BEC relations among π0π0, π±π±, π+π−, and π±π0 systems.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024, experimental verification of GBEC at high energies is still considered a prospect.
